messages.author: e21d6ba8abd772f8
messages.subject: Comparing distance estimates
parts:
For my graduate work I am comparing densities of different bird specie=
s on burned and unburned grasslands where I surveyed avian communities usin=
g point counts over multiple years. Due to low numbers of detections per pl=
ot per species (<15) I am unable to get reliable density estimates for each=
plot using DISTANCE and needed to pool all detections to get a single dens=
ity estimate. I cannot compare these two estimates using standard statistic=
al techniques due to the log-normal distribution of the density estimate. I=
s there any formula or other type of test to be able to do this?
I am thinking about trying methods used by Marcus et al. 2000 (Wilson =
Bulletin 112:517-523) with detection probabilities from DISTANCE. They used=
counts from each plot, also with low sample sizes, and divided those by de=
tection probabilities then by the area surveyed. Then I can use individual =
plot density estimates and standard statistical tests. Thanks for any help,=
comments, or suggestions.
Tony Roberts

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Comparing distance estimates
parts:
Tony:

I can't speak to the Wilson Bulletin paper you cite, but presuming you
pool detections to get some sort of common detection function from which
to produce your detection probabilities, you have lost the independence
among your points, and they are not longer true replicates.

As an alternative, a forthcoming paper in the Journal of Biological and
Ecological Statistics speaks directly to your setup (burned/unburned
comparison, point transects, multiple years). It is not yet in print,
but a preprint is posted on Prof. Buckland's website.

http://www.creem.st-and.ac.uk/stb/buckland%20et%20al%20jabes%202008.pdf

Roberts, Tony wrote:

> > For my graduate work I am comparing densities of different bird species on burned and unburned grasslands where I surveyed avian communities using point counts over multiple years. Due to low numbers of detections per plot per species (<15) I am unable to get reliable density estimates for each plot using DISTANCE and needed to pool all detections to get a single density estimate. I cannot compare these two estimates using standard statistical techniques due to the log-normal distribution of the density estimate. Is there any formula or other type of test to be able to do this?
> > I am thinking about trying methods used by Marcus et al. 2000 (Wilson Bulletin 112:517-523) with detection probabilities from DISTANCE. They used counts from each plot, also with low sample sizes, and divided those by detection probabilities then by the area surveyed. Then I can use individual plot density estimates and standard statistical tests. Thanks for any help, comments, or suggestions.
